[INFERENCE] Coal plants of this scale in Poland are invariably served by rail infrastructure, as rail is the primary mode for bulk coal transport in the Polish energy sector. [FACT] The plant is located in Połaniec, Świętokrzyskie Province, which is connected to Poland's standard-gauge (1435mm) railway network. [INFERENCE] The existing rail infrastructure that delivered millions of tonnes of coal over 45+ years of operation is more than adequate for delivering segmented SMR modules totaling ~700 tonnes. The estimated transport capability significantly exceeds the threshold requirement, therefore the site passes this criterion with high confidence.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island, with 72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint. [FACT] Polaniec power station is a large coal facility with 1882 MWe installed capacity, making it one of Poland's largest thermal power plants. [INFERENCE] Based on typical coal plant area requirements of 0.05-0.15 ha/MWe, a facility of this size would occupy approximately 94-282 ha, well exceeding both the 14 ha minimum and 72.8 ha preferred thresholds. [FACT] The plant is located in Połaniec, Świętokrzyskie Province, in a rural/industrial area along the Vistula River with significant industrial land use. [INFERENCE] Large Polish coal plants of this vintage and capacity typically have substantial site areas to accommodate multiple units, coal handling facilities, ash disposal areas, and cooling infrastructure. The estimated site area of 94-282 ha significantly exceeds the 14 ha minimum threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion with substantial margin.

[NS-05 web_search v1.3-2026-04-18] Status: operating. Site area: 188 ha (buildable: 150 ha, expansion: 50 ha). Confidence: low. Sources: https://www.gem.wiki/Polaniec_power_station; https://pl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enea_Elektrownia_Po%C5%82aniec; https://www.enea.pl/pl/grupaenea/o-grupie/spolki-grupy-enea/polaniec/ochrona-srodowiska-i-bezpieczenstwo-otoczenia/gospodarka-odpadami. FACT: Plant is operating with 1882 MW capacity across eight coal/biomass units. ESTIMATE: No official area data found despite searches of GDOS, Enea documents, and Polish media. Using capacity proxy of 0.10 ha/MW typical for Polish coal plants yields 188 ha estimate. INFERENCE: Buildable area reduced to 150 ha assuming 20% constraint from active rail, cooling ponds. INFERENCE: Expansion potential of 50 ha based on ash disposal areas mentioned in waste management documents, though specific area not quantified. Confidence low due to lack of official documentation.

The threshold for population density avoidance is < 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The Polaniec power station is located in Połaniec, Świętokrzyskie Voivodeship, Poland, in a predominantly rural area along the Vistula River. [ESTIMATE] The town of Połaniec has approximately 8,000-9,000 inhabitants and is the primary settlement within the 5 km radius. [INFERENCE] Given the rural character of the Świętokrzyskie region and the typical siting of Polish coal plants away from major urban centers, the surrounding area within 5 km consists mainly of agricultural land and small villages with very low population density. [ESTIMATE] The estimated total population within the 5 km radius is approximately 10,000-12,000 persons, yielding a density of approximately 127-153 persons/km² (total population ÷ 78.5 km²). This estimated density is well below the 1,000 persons/km² threshold, providing substantial margin for the avoidance criterion.

llm_verdicts.llm_justification: [FACT] Polaniec power station is located in the Sandomierz Basin/Vistula River valley with Quaternary alluvial cover over Neogene sediments. [INFERENCE] The site is not on soluble bedrock (carbonates/evaporites) where karst could form, but rather on clastic basin fill typical of coal plant locations. [INFERENCE] Massive karst formation is geologically impossible at this location, so the exclusionary threshold is not triggered. [UNKNOWN] Site-specific geological survey data would provide definitive bedrock confirmation, but the river valley setting strongly indicates non-karstic conditions.
llm_verdicts.llm_sources_needed: Site-specific geological survey data; Detailed geological maps at 1:25,000 scale; Borehole logs confirming bedrock lithology
